answer: Each identity holds a short-lived capability token that only a randomly assigned peer can issue after the identity completes a small verifiable job, like re-checking a data sample. Tokens expire every epoch and sit on a narrow ledge: they cannot be stockpiled, transferred, or minted in bulk. Every token carries a unique pigment of the job it came from, so a verifier can trace it back to real work, and each token is sealed with a cipher binding it to one identity. A farm of ten thousand clones must redo ten thousand fresh jobs every epoch, while one honest agent does one.
